title: Advanced CI/CD Architecture Patterns knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement correctly describes Advanced CI/CD Architecture Patterns?
options: Print all environment variables and event payloads to make the run easier to debug.
Run untrusted pull-request code in the same job that holds production credentials.
Advanced architectures use explicit stages, fan-out/fan-in, cross-repository events, build-once/deploy-many, and separate build privileges from production credentials.
Give every job write permission to avoid troubleshooting authorization errors.
questions.answer_key: Advanced architectures use explicit stages, fan-out/fan-in, cross-repository events, build-once/deploy-many, and separate build privileges from production credentials.
questions.explanation: This is the central behavior of advanced ci/cd architecture patterns: Advanced architectures use explicit stages, fan-out/fan-in, cross-repository events, build-once/deploy-many, and separate build privileges from production credentials. Validate configuration and behavior against the current official reference before production use.

questions.prompt: A team is working with “Multi-stage pipelines”. Which practice best fits this topic?
options: Use filters to reduce unnecessary runs only when skipped work is genuinely unrelated. Include shared dependencies and test the changed and unchanged path cases so required checks are not bypassed.
Give every job write permission to avoid troubleshooting authorization errors.
Print all environment variables and event payloads to make the run easier to debug.
Run untrusted pull-request code in the same job that holds production credentials.
questions.answer_key: Use filters to reduce unnecessary runs only when skipped work is genuinely unrelated. Include shared dependencies and test the changed and unchanged path cases so required checks are not bypassed.
questions.explanation: Multi-stage pipelines: Use filters to reduce unnecessary runs only when skipped work is genuinely unrelated. Include shared dependencies and test the changed and unchanged path cases so required checks are not bypassed. Apply the guidance to the actual event, runner, permissions, or artifact boundary and test the relevant case.

questions.prompt: How should a reviewer verify a change related to advanced ci/cd architecture patterns?
options: Retry every failure without looking at the exit code or preserving evidence.
Publish the workflow to production before reviewing its triggers and permissions.
Run a controlled test or static check, inspect the relevant job and step result, and compare the evidence with the stated acceptance criteria.
Assume the workflow is correct as soon as the YAML file is committed.
questions.answer_key: Run a controlled test or static check, inspect the relevant job and step result, and compare the evidence with the stated acceptance criteria.
questions.explanation: Reliable verification uses observable evidence. For this lesson, consider: Advanced architectures use explicit stages, fan-out/fan-in, cross-repository events, build-once/deploy-many, and separate build privileges from production credentials. A syntax check alone cannot prove remote execution, permissions, or deployment behavior.
